hypotheses.title: The layered ICE Air chain creates a visibility failure beyond ordinary prime/subcontract structure and routine lawful redaction
hypotheses.description: The combined public-recipient, subaward, operator, asset, and support records systematically fail to expose downstream economic and operational attribution in a way ordinary contracting and ordinary redaction do not adequately explain. This is a visibility hypothesis, not an allegation of illegality, intent, or improper concealment.
hypotheses.falsification: Falsified if the governing award files show that CSI is accurately reported as the legal recipient; downstream reporting obligations were satisfied or did not apply; participant disclosures and ordinary joins recover the material support/operator layers; and redactions map to documented, segregability-tested procurement, proprietary, privacy, safety, or operational grounds while internal rosters reconcile to performance and payments.
hypotheses.predicted_evidence: Mandatory-but-missing or materially incomplete FSRS reports; inconsistent recipient/vendor ledgers; releasable carrier or payment fields withheld without a supported basis; irreconcilable operator, tail, invoice, and asset records; or repeated omission of material downstream amounts after ordinary structured joins.

hypotheses.title: Ordinary prime/subcontract architecture plus routine lawful redaction and reporting limits adequately explains the public record
hypotheses.description: ICE properly reports CSI as the legal prime and order recipient; CSI coordinates a full service using carriers and support vendors; participants and official sources disclose some downstream roles; public subaward coverage is incomplete or inapplicable; and operational/proprietary records are lawfully redacted or not routinely published.
hypotheses.falsification: Falsified if applicable reporting rules required material subcontract disclosure that was not made; agency records cannot reconcile the listed carriers, aircraft, invoices, and performance; redaction logs fail to identify a sustainable basis or ignore segregable identity-neutral fields; or downstream payments and roles remain materially unrecoverable even from the ordinary contract, FSRS, invoice, and COR records that should contain them.
hypotheses.predicted_evidence: A complete accountable prime record; FSRS reports or a documented exemption/non-applicability determination; internally complete operator/tail/preflight records; ordinary vendor invoices and subcontract-consent files; and supported redactions with segregable release of non-sensitive carrier, certificate, aircraft, and aggregate payment fields.

dependency_clusters.treatment: one issuer/document family; not three independent contradictions
one federal reporting family; multiple instruments but not independent source corroboration
paired termination/reinstatement chronology; neutral on downstream visibility
same issuer family; direct contract edge and general operator capability are distinct propositions but not independent corroboration
agreement and closing sequence; ownership only
one unresolved operational-record gap; zero tails is a result derived from the same missing/redacted record layer

verdict.statement: H0 is least inconsistent, not confirmed. The public record has a practical reconstruction gap, but the current verified evidence does not make that gap diagnostically attributable to anything beyond ordinary prime/subcontract architecture, coverage limits, and redacted operational records.
verdict.important_limit: The record does not establish that every redaction is lawful or that every reporting obligation was satisfied; those are untested assumptions of H0, not findings.

against_H1: CSI is directly visible as the legal BPA/order recipient (#12895, #12899, #12910).
GEO publicly disclosed GTI's CSI subcontract and a bounded annualized revenue estimate (#12892-#12894).
GlobalX publicly disclosed a current CSI/U.S.-government contract through 2026 (#12976).
An official state source names GlobalX and Eastern as ICE flight providers (#12978), while the House letter names GlobalX beneath CSI with a reporting-derived limitation (#12912).
GTI appears in federal recipient data when it is actually the legal prime on a separate direct contract (#12909).
not_currently_diagnostic: Zero public subaward rows (#12901) without a reporting-duty, exemption, waiver, or correction record.
Redacted replacement carrier/aircraft documents (#12981) without the redaction basis or segregability analysis.
Zero confirmed tails, because fleet inventories and authority do not prove assignment and the decisive operational records are missing.
Eastern's official ICE edge without a CSI edge (#12978), because both a separate legal path and an undisclosed ordinary subcontract remain possible.
CSI's ownership of Air Wisconsin/13 CRJ200s (#12979-#12980), because capability is not assignment.

exact_discriminators.record: FSRS applicability and compliance file for the five exact orders/calls
exact_discriminators.supports_H1_if: reporting was mandatory and material subcontract rows are missing, incomplete, or inconsistent without a documented correction
exact_discriminators.supports_H0_if: reports reconcile or the file documents a valid exemption, non-applicability determination, or other ordinary coverage reason

exact_discriminators.record: Unredacted or segregable Classic Air administrative-record Tabs 91, 92b, 94, and 101 plus the withholding/redaction basis
exact_discriminators.supports_H1_if: identity-neutral carrier, certificate, aircraft, or aggregate commitment fields were withheld without a sustainable basis or conflict with actual performance
exact_discriminators.supports_H0_if: the package reconciles to performance and redactions are supported, limited, and segregability-tested

exact_discriminators.record: CSI-GTI subcontract, current carrier teaming/subcontract agreements, consent file, amendments, invoices, and vendor ledger
exact_discriminators.supports_H1_if: material payees, roles, or amounts cannot be reconciled to required reports and ordinary company/agency records
exact_discriminators.supports_H0_if: the chain and payments reconcile to the legal-prime record and ordinary downstream accounting

exact_discriminators.record: Call 70CDCR26FC0000001 preflight and flight-leg records with operating-carrier certificate, N-number, mission date/type, and no personal crew identifiers
exact_discriminators.supports_H1_if: required records are absent, internally inconsistent, or identity-neutral fields remain unjustifiably unavailable
exact_discriminators.supports_H0_if: the authoritative roster exists, reconciles to operators and invoices, and only legitimately sensitive fields are withheld

exact_discriminators.record: CSI's response and production to the 2025-05-28 House Homeland Security letter
exact_discriminators.supports_H1_if: the production reveals material undisclosed layers or unexplained discrepancies
exact_discriminators.supports_H0_if: subcontracts and monthly counts reconcile to the prime, carrier disclosures, and ICE records

premortem.if_verdict_is_wrong: The analysis may be over-crediting voluntary company disclosures and treating unknown reporting/redaction rules as benign. A visible edge can coexist with material hidden payments or operational substitutions.
premortem.fastest_check: Obtain the FSRS applicability/compliance file and an identity-neutral extract of the current flight-leg/preflight roster, then reconcile both to CSI's vendor ledger and carrier invoices.
